# Duriath Helbane

*Pages PDF 121-122*

Patrons and nemeses 

## **Duriath Helbane**
_‘By the Dragons Below, if you spill one more drop of that Sapherian wine, I’ll see you and your family dissected alive by the high beastmaster before dawn!’_ 

— Fleetmaster Helbane 

**Motivation:** To become Malerion’s greatest fleetmaster **Short-term ambition:** Uncover and eliminate threats to his position on _Temple of Spite_ 

**Long-term ambition:** Fulfil his promises to Anethra Helbane and Malerion 

**Impress Anethra Helbane.** The matriarch has great expectations of Duriath. He made bold promises of conquering Tor Elithis, which he now must fulfill. He has Anethra’s support for now, but she will tear him down if disappointed. 

**Win Malerion’s support.** Helbane pledged to Malerion that Tor Elithis would fall within ten years. Now he has five years left, and the Dread King has yet to offer any military or other aid. 

**Conquer Tor Elithis.** Many of Helbane’s ambitions are in service of his grand endeavour. Should the Asur outpost fall, he will make his mark on history. 

Ruling a black ark is like walking along a sword blade in full armour, over a sea of ravening helldrakes. Every decree must land with precision, every alliance weighed against betrayal, and every show of strength must be calculated to silence whispers of weakness. Duriath Helbane is burdened by his ambitions and the knowledge that loyalty is merely a mask for ambition. He may be the tyrant of _Temple of Spite_ , but it brings no satisfaction. 

The Helbanes are a noble house of Clar Karond, overshadowed by their still-living matriarch, Anethra Helbane. Her countless offspring compete for their inheritance, united only by threats from other lineages, especially rival nobles from Karond Kar. From youth, Duriath wanted to escape the claustrophobic politics of Clar Karond, so in 1820 IC, he joined a corsair company attached to _Temple of Spite_ . He enjoyed the freedom of life at sea, before he was castigated by Anethra for wasting his place in society. Duly chastened, he plotted and backstabbed his way to the Reavers’ Council, before seizing control of the ark from his cousin Dravia, by marooning her on the Dragon Isles off the coast of Lustria. Duriath knows his own position is as precarious as Dravia’s, and the recent mutiny was a timely reminder of the perils of Druchii command. 

Duriath Helbane is insanely ambitious and struggles to prioritise his plans: 

**Enforce complete control of the ark.** Helbane tolerates no dissent or disobedience. He cannot see into every corridor and chamber, but he deploys secret investigators to root out potential threats to his dominion. This includes keeping the irreverent Khainites under control. 

**Strengthen his armed forces.** To assault Tor Elithis, the warhost must double in size, the fleet must expand, the treasury must overflow. Helbane wants no excuses, he wants his demands met. 

**Humiliate Lokhir Fellheart.** The Helbanes are rivals of the Fellhearts of Clar Karond and Duriath has an acute loathing for the Krakenlord and his accomplishments. Duriath has always been in Lokhir’s shadow, and yearns to eclipse him. 

Helbane’s days are frenetic,  he feigns the languor of an effortless commander, but it is deception. He wakes early, summons his servants, and issues demands and punishments at a rapid pace. Highborn, reavers, and others are pulled into his throne room on a whim, ordered on some new task, and then dismissed. Every notion creates a cascade of new work, recriminations, and suffering the further down the hierarchy it passes. On occasion, Helbane abandons his original idea and demands to know why everyone is wasting their time following his previous directions when his new orders are clearly more important. 

Behind his tyranny is an uncomfortable truth that no amount of punishment flayings can hide: Duriath Helbane has overpromised to Anethra and Malerion. 

## **Duriath Helbane as Nemesis**
Helbane is a natural nemesis, the ultimate commander of the floating nightmare that is _Temple of Spite_ . If he hears of attempts to subvert his authority or sink the ark, he stops at nothing to end them. He rarely gets his hands dirty, but relies on warriors such as Vaelith’s Blackswords or Guardmaster Vranek Umberkill to chase down any threat. 

Whatever their intentions, he may assume they are working for disloyal members of the Black Convocation, Karond Kar, or Lokhir Fellheart. He doesn’t need a good reason to persecute anyone.

**Sword** (90/+8) 

Duriath Helbane has ash-grey skin and piercing green eyes like fishscales. His voice is stark and deeper than most elves, it has no music or lightness at all. He is possessed of an intense presence and a restless energy, and has a habit of tapping the pommel of his cutlass on the furniture as he talks. The only time he seems relaxed is when reminiscing of his days as a humble corsair. He has a wife and children back in Clar Karond, who he gives little thought and has not seen for several decades. Duriath has an ongoing dalliance with Saerith the Bladed, who is trying to inveigle him into the Cult of Slaanesh, to embrace pleasure as an escape from his gnawing doubts. 

## **Duriath Helbane as Patron**
Duriath Helbane has more important ambitions than rounding up every escaped captive. If he learns about the Characters on the ark, his mind will turn to advantage… they could prove useful before he has them killed. 

Helbane can trust very few of his vassals to help him root out dissent, and the party could be useful as a team of disposable assets to investigate on his behalf, provided his name is kept out of it. If need be, he can furnish them with plausible employment as servants to help. 

He might order them to accompany Valerion’s Blackswords to seek the Impossible Prism in Tlax (see page 75). Or he could suggest they discover Lokhir Fellheart’s whereabouts and attempt to humiliate him, for what better way to damage the Krakenlord’s reputation than seeing him outwitted by a wretched bunch of adventurers? 

**Repeater Handbow and Bolts:** (75/+6) range of 10 yards with the _Impale_ , _Pistol_ , and _Repeater 3_ Qualities, and the _Reload 9_ Flaw
